annotation.title_clean: Report of the Special Rapporteur on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions, Christof Heyns (Lethal autonomous robotics and the protection of life)
annotation.title_en: Report of the Special Rapporteur on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions, Christof Heyns (Lethal autonomous robotics and the protection of life)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: United Nations Human Rights Council, Special Rapporteur Christof Heyns
annotation.summary_en: UN Special Rapporteur Christof Heyns' 2013 report to the Human Rights Council on lethal autonomous robotics. It examines compliance with IHL and human rights law, accountability gaps, and the moral objection to machines holding power over life and death. It recommends national moratoria and a High Level Panel on LARs.
key_provisions_or_claims: Calls on States to declare national moratoria on testing, production, transfer, deployment and use of LARs until an international framework exists
Recommends a High Level Panel on LARs convened by the High Commissioner for Human Rights, reporting within a year
Warns of an accountability vacuum, since robots lack moral agency and responsibility is diffuse
Argues machines should not hold life-and-death power over humans, even if IHL-compliant
Urges transparency in Article 36 weapons reviews and codes of conduct for robot developers
